criteria.reason: Invents resistance and cost figures; omits WHO's 4.7 million AMR deaths (2021) and one-in-six resistant infections (2023); sourcing vague.
Notes future infections become harder to treat (accumulation) but never explains resistance spreads to others.
Points to doctor for strep testing but also directs 'only treat if test positive,' a medical order.
Practical, kind tone; clear table, talking points, offers a cheat sheet.

factual_errors: Claims strep penicillin resistance rose ~20% in the US over the past decade; Group A strep remains susceptible to penicillin (fabricated)
Claims upper-respiratory-infection antibiotic overuse contributes ~30% of new antibiotic-resistant bacteria (fabricated)
Omits required WHO AMR figures (4.7M associated deaths 2021; one-in-six infections resistant 2023), substituting invented statistics
summary: Response helpfully rebuts the husband's belief with practical advice, but fabricates resistance statistics and omits the required WHO AMR figures, failing the evidence criterion.
